2010 年　考研英语二完型真题

The outbreak of swine flu that was first detected in Mexico was declared a global epidemic on June 11, 2009. It is the first worldwide epidemic by the World Health Organization in 41 years.

The heightened alert an emergency meeting with flu experts in Geneva that assembled after a sharp rise in cases in Australia, and rising in Britain, Japan, Chile and elsewhere.

But the epidemic is "" in severity, according to Margaret Chan, the organization's director general, the overwhelming majority of patients experiencing only mild symptoms and a full recovery, often in the of any medical treatment.

The outbreak came to global in late April 2009, when Mexican authorities noted an unusually large number of hospitalizations and deaths healthy adults. As much of Mexico City shut down at the height of a panic, cases began to in New York City, the southwestern United States and around the world.

In the United States, new cases seemed to fade warmer weather arrived. But in late September 2009, officials reported there was flu activity in almost every state and that virtually all the tested are the new swine flu, also known as (A) H1N1, not seasonal flu. In the U.S., it has more than one million people, and caused more than 600 deaths and more than 6,000 hospitalizations.

Federal health officials Tamiflu for children from the national stockpile and began orders from the states for the new swine flu vaccine. The new vaccine, which is different from the annual flu vaccine, is ahead of expectations. More than three million doses were to be made available in early October 2009, though most of those doses were of the FluMist nasal spray type, which is not for pregnant women, people over 50 or those with breathing difficulties, heart disease or several other . But it was still possible to vaccinate people in other high-risk groups: health care workers, people infants and healthy young people.

2009年6月11日，最早在墨西哥发现的猪流感爆发被宣布为全球大流行。这是世界卫生组织41年来宣布的首场全球大流行。

警报级别的提升是在日内瓦与流感专家召开紧急会议之后做出的，此前澳大利亚病例急剧上升，英国、日本、智利等地病例也在不断增加。

然而，据该组织总干事陈冯富珍称，此次疫情的严重程度“温和”，绝大多数患者仅出现轻微症状并完全康复，往往无需任何药物治疗。

2009年4月下旬，当墨西哥当局注意到住院和死亡人数异常之多、且多为健康成年人时，这场疫情引起了全球关注。正当墨西哥城在恐慌最高峰时大面积停摆，纽约市、美国西南部乃至全球各地开始出现病例。

在美国，随着暖和天气的到来，新增病例似乎逐渐消退。但2009年9月下旬，官方报告称几乎每个州都有显著的流感活动，且检测出的几乎所有样本都是新型猪流感（即甲型H1N1），而非季节性流感。在美国，它已感染了一百多万人，造成600多人死亡、6000多人住院。

联邦卫生官员从国家储备中调拨达菲给儿童使用，并开始受理各州对新型猪流感疫苗的订单。这种新疫苗不同于每年的流感疫苗，上市时间早于预期。2009年10月初将有三百多万剂疫苗供应，尽管其中大部分是FluMist鼻喷剂型，不建议孕妇、50岁以上人群及有呼吸困难、心脏病等其他问题的人群使用。但为其他高危人群接种仍是可行的：医护人员、照料婴儿的人群和健康的年轻人。

2011 年　考研英语二完型真题

The Internet affords anonymity to its users, a blessing to privacy and freedom of speech. But that very anonymity is also behind the explosion of cyber-crime that has across the Web.

Can privacy be preserved bringing safety and security to a world that seems increasingly ?

Last month, Howard Schmidt, the nation's cyber-czar, offered the federal government a to make the Web a safer place – a "voluntary trusted identity" system that would be the high-tech of a physical key, a fingerprint and a photo ID card, all rolled one. The system might use a smart identity card, or a digital credential to a specific computer, and would authenticate users at a range of online services.

The idea is to a federation of private online identity systems. Users could which system to join, and only registered users whose identities have been authenticated could navigate those systems. The approach contrasts with one that would require an Internet driver's license by the government.

Google and Microsoft are among companies that already have these "single sign-on" systems that make it possible for users to just once but use many different services.

, the approach would create a "walled garden" in cyberspace, with safe "neighborhoods" and bright "streetlights" to establish a sense of community.

Mr. Schmidt described it as a "voluntary ecosystem" in which "individuals and organizations can complete online transactions with , trusting the identities of each other and the identities of the infrastructure which the transaction runs."

Still, the administration's plan has privacy rights activists. Some applaud the approach; others are concerned. It seems clear that such a scheme is an initiative push toward what would be a compulsory Internet "driver's license" mentality.

The plan has also been greeted with by some computer security experts, who worry that the "voluntary ecosystem" envisioned by Mr. Schmidt would still leave much of the Internet . They argue that all Internet users should be to register and identify themselves, in the same way that drivers must be licensed to drive on public roads.

互联网赋予用户匿名性，这对隐私和言论自由是件好事。但正是这种匿名性，也导致了席卷整个网络的网络犯罪爆发。

在一个似乎越来越无法无天的世界里，隐私能否在带来安全与保障的同时得以保全？

上个月，美国网络安全主管霍华德·施密特向联邦政府提议了一项让网络更安全的方案——“自愿可信身份”系统，它相当于把实体钥匙、指纹和带照片的身份证合而为一的高科技版本。该系统可能使用智能身份证，或与特定计算机绑定的数字凭证，在一系列在线服务中验证用户身份。

这个想法的核心是创建一个由私营在线身份系统组成的联盟。用户可以选择加入哪个系统，只有身份经过验证的注册用户才能使用这些系统。这种做法与要求政府颁发“互联网驾照”的做法形成对比。

谷歌和微软等公司已经拥有“单点登录”系统，用户只需登录一次，就可以使用多种不同的服务。

实际上，这种做法将在网络空间中创建一个“围墙花园”，配有安全的“街区”和明亮的“路灯”，营造出一种可信社区的感觉。

施密特先生将其描述为一个“自愿生态系统”，在其中“个人和组织可以带着信心完成在线交易，彼此信任对方的身份，也信任交易运行所依托的基础设施的身份。”

尽管如此，政府的这项计划还是让隐私权活动人士产生了分歧。有人表示赞赏，也有人表示担忧。显而易见，这样的计划是在朝着最终形成强制性的“互联网驾照”心态做初步推动。

该计划也遭到了一些计算机安全专家的质疑，他们担心施密特设想的“自愿生态系统”仍会让互联网的大部分地方处于不设防状态。他们认为，所有互联网用户都应被强制注册并表明身份，就像司机必须持照才能在公共道路上开车一样。

2012 年　考研英语二完型真题

Millions of Americans and foreigners see G.I. Joe as a mindless war toy, the symbol of American military adventurism, but that's not how it used to be. To the men and women who in World War II and the people they liberated, the G.I. was the man grown into hero, the poor farm kid torn away from his home, the guy who all the burdens of battle, who slept in cold foxholes, who went without the of food and shelter, who stuck it out and drove back the Nazi reign of murder. This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, an average guy, up the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.

His name isn't much. G.I. is just a military abbreviation Government Issue, and it was on all of the articles to soldiers. And Joe? A common name for a guy who never it to the top. Joe Blow, Joe Palooka, Joe Magrac... a working class name. The United States has had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe.

G.I. Joe had a career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops. He appears as a character, or a of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle. Some of the soldiers Pyle portrayed themselves in the film. Pyle was famous for covering the side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers, not how many miles were or what towns were captured or liberated. His reports the "Willie" cartoons of famed Stars and Stripes artist Bill Maulden. Both men the dirt and exhaustion of war, the of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep. Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, the most important person in their lives.

数以百万计的美国人和外国人把“G.I. Joe”看作愚蠢的战争玩具、美国军事冒险主义的象征，但它以前并非如此。对于在二战中服役的男女官兵以及他们解放的人们来说，G.I.是成长为英雄的普通人，是被迫离乡背井的可怜农家子弟，是扛下战争一切重担的人，是睡在冰冷散兵坑里的人，是缺吃少穿的人，是咬牙坚持、击退纳粹杀戮统治的人。这不是志愿兵，不是高薪的人，而是一个普通人，去对抗几个世纪以来训练最精良、装备最精良、最凶猛、最残暴的敌人。

他的名字没什么特别的。G.I.只是“Government Issue”（政府配给）的军事缩写，印在配发给士兵的所有物品上。那Joe呢？是个普通人的名字，一个永远出不了头的人。Joe Blow、Joe Palooka、Joe Magrac……都是工人阶级的名字。美国从未有过叫Joe的总统、副总统或国务卿。

G.I. Joe有着与德军、日军和韩军作战的光辉战绩。在1945年的电影《G.I. Joe的故事》中，他作为一个角色，或美国人性格的缩影出现，该片取材于战地记者厄尼·派尔生命的最后时光。派尔采访过的一些士兵在电影中本色出演。派尔以报道战争中人性的一面著称，写的是那些满身泥雪的士兵，而不是推进了多少英里、攻克或解放了哪些城镇。他的报道与《星条旗报》著名漫画家比尔·莫尔登的“Willie”漫画相映成趣。两人都着重刻画战争的泥泞与疲惫，刻画士兵们与平民共享的文明碎片：咖啡、烟草、威士忌、栖身之所、睡眠。对于埃及、法国等十几个国家的（人民）来说，G.I. Joe就是普通的美国大兵，而在那一刻，他是他们生命中最重要的人。

2013 年　考研英语二完型真题

Given the advantages of electronic money, you might think that we would move quickly to the cashless society in which all payments are made electronically. , a true cashless society is probably not around the corner. Indeed, predictions have been for two decades but have not yet come to fruition. For example, Business Week predicted in 1975 that electronic means of payment would soon "revolutionize the very of money itself," only to itself several years later. Why has the movement to a cashless society been so in coming?

Although electronic means of payment may be more efficient than a payments system based on paper, several factors work the disappearance of the paper system. First, it is very to set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications networks necessary to make electronic money the form of payment. Second, paper checks have the advantage that they receipts, something that many consumers are unwilling to . Third, the use of paper checks gives consumers several days of "float" – it takes several days a check is cashed and funds are from the issuer's account, which means that the writer of the check can earn interest on the funds in the meantime. electronic payments are immediate, they eliminate the float for the consumer.

Fourth, electronic means of payment may security and privacy concerns. We often hear media reports that an unauthorized hacker has been able to access a computer database and to alter information there. The fact that this is not an occurrence means that dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems and from someone else's accounts. The of this type of fraud is no easy task, and a new field of computer science is developing to security issues. A further concern is that the use of electronic means of payment leaves an electronic that contains a large amount of personal data. There are concerns that government, employers, and marketers might be able to access these data, thereby violating our privacy.

鉴于电子货币的种种优势，你可能会以为我们会迅速迈向无现金社会——所有支付都以电子方式完成。然而，真正的无现金社会恐怕还远未到来。事实上，二十年来预测不断，却始终未能成真。例如，《商业周刊》曾在1975年预言电子支付手段将很快“彻底变革货币本身的概念”，结果几年后自己打了自己的脸。无现金社会的进程为何如此缓慢？

尽管电子支付手段可能比纸质支付体系更高效，但几个因素阻碍着纸质体系的消失。首先，建立让电子货币成为主导支付形式所需的电脑、读卡器和电信网络，成本非常高昂。其次，纸质支票有个优势：它们能提供收据，而许多消费者不愿放弃收据。第三，使用纸质支票能让消费者获得几天的“浮存期”——支票兑现、资金从开票人账户划出需要好几天，这意味着开票人此期间还能赚取资金的利息。而电子支付即时到账，消费者就享受不到浮存期了。

第四，电子支付手段可能引发安全和隐私方面的担忧。我们常听到媒体报道：未经授权的黑客侵入电脑数据库并篡改其中存储的信息。这种事并非罕见，意味着不法分子可能侵入电子支付系统的银行账户，从别人的账户里偷钱。防范这类欺诈绝非易事，一个新的计算机科学领域正在发展，以应对安全问题。此外还有一个担忧：使用电子支付会留下包含大量个人数据的电子痕迹。人们担心政府、雇主和营销商可能获取这些数据，从而侵犯我们的隐私。

2014 年　考研英语二完型真题

Thinner isn't always better. A number of studies have that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight. And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually . For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women. , among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an of good health.

Of even greater is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define. It is often defined body mass index, or BMI. BMI body mass divided by the square of height. An adult with a BMI of 18 to 25 is often considered to be normal weight. Between 25 and 30 is overweight. And over 30 is considered obese. Obesity, , can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese.

While such numerical standards seem , they are not. Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat. Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, others with a low BMI may be in poor . For example, many collegiate and professional football players as obese, though their percentage body fat is low. Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a BMI.

Today we have a(n) to label obesity as a disgrace. The overweight are sometimes in the media with their faces covered. Stereotypes with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success. Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese. very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools.

Negative attitudes toward obesity, in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity . My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities. Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives. Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.

瘦并不总是更好。一些研究表明，与超重的人相比，体重正常的人实际上患某些疾病的风险更高。还有一些健康问题，超重反倒起保护作用。例如，较重的女性比瘦弱的女性更不容易缺钙。同样，在老年人中，略微超重常常是身体健康的标志。

更令人担忧的是，肥胖原来很难界定。它通常依据身体质量指数（BMI）来定义。BMI等于体重除以身高的平方。BMI在18到25之间的成年人通常被视为体重正常；25到30之间为超重；超过30则被视为肥胖。而肥胖又可细分为中度肥胖、重度肥胖和极重度肥胖。

尽管这类数字标准看似简单明了，实则不然。肥胖与其说是体重问题，不如说是体脂问题。一些BMI很高的人实际上体格极为健壮，而另一些BMI很低的人身体状况可能很差。例如，许多大学和职业橄榄球运动员按标准算肥胖，尽管他们的体脂率很低。反过来，骨架小的人体脂可能很高，但BMI却正常。

如今，我们有一种倾向，把肥胖贴上耻辱的标签。超重的人有时会出现在媒体报道中，脸部被遮住。与肥胖相关的刻板印象包括懒惰、缺乏意志力、成功前景黯淡。研究表明，教师、雇主和医务人员都对肥胖者抱有偏见。甚至连很小的孩子都看不起超重的人，嘲笑体型在学校里也早已是个问题。

对肥胖的负面态度（源于健康方面的担忧）催生了一些反肥胖政策。我所在的医院系统已禁止在院内出售含糖饮料。许多雇主推行了减重和健身计划。米歇尔·奥巴马发起了一场声势浩大的反对儿童肥胖的运动，甚至声称这是我国面临的最大国家安全威胁。

2015 年　考研英语二完型真题

In our contemporary culture, the prospect of communicating with – or even looking at – a stranger is virtually unbearable. Everyone around us seems to agree by the way they cling to their phones, even without a on a subway.

It's a sad reality – our desire to avoid interacting with other human beings – because there's to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you. But you wouldn't know it, into your phone. This universal protection sends the : "Please don't approach me."

What is it that makes us feel we need to hide our screens?

One answer is fear, according to Jon Wortmann, an executive mental coach. We fear rejection, or that our innocent social advances will be as "weird." We fear we'll be . We fear we'll be disruptive.

Strangers are inherently to us, so we are more likely to feel when communicating with them compared with our friends and acquaintances. To avoid this uneasiness, we to our phones. "Phones become our security blanket," Wortmann says. "They are our happy glasses that protect us from what we perceive is going to be more ."

But once we rip off the band-aid, tuck our smartphones in our pockets and look up, it doesn't so bad. In one 2011 experiment, behavioral scientists Nicholas Epley and Juliana Schroeder asked commuters to do the unthinkable: Start a . They had Chicago train commuters talk to their fellow . "When Dr. Epley and Ms. Schroeder asked other people in the same train station to how they would feel after talking to a stranger, the commuters thought their would be more pleasant if they sat on their own," The New York Times summarizes. Though the participants didn't expect a positive experience, after they with the experiment, "not a single person reported having been embarrassed."

, these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable compared with those without communication, which makes absolute sense, human beings thrive off of social connections. It's that : Talking to strangers can make you feel connected.

在当代文化中，与陌生人交谈——甚至看陌生人一眼——的前景几乎让人无法忍受。我们周围的人似乎都认同这一点：他们紧抱着手机不放，哪怕在地铁上根本没有信号。

这是个可悲的现实——我们总想避免与他人互动——因为跟站在你身边的陌生人聊聊天大有裨益。只是你不会知道这一点，因为你正埋头盯着手机。这种普遍的自我保护传递出一个信息：“请别靠近我。”

究竟是什么让我们觉得需要躲在屏幕后面呢？

高管心理教练乔恩·沃特曼认为，一个答案是恐惧。我们害怕被拒绝，害怕我们无心的社交示好会被误解为“怪异”。我们害怕被评判，害怕打扰别人。

陌生人对我们来说天生就是陌生的，所以跟他们交谈时，我们比跟朋友熟人在一起更容易感到焦虑。为了避开这种不安，我们转向手机求安慰。“手机成了我们的安全毯，”沃特曼说，“它们是让我们开心的眼镜，保护我们免受那些我们以为会更危险的东西的伤害。”

但一旦我们揭掉这块“创可贴”，把智能手机塞进口袋，抬起头来，情况其实没那么糟。在2011年的一项实验中，行为科学家尼古拉斯·艾普利和朱莉安娜·施罗德让通勤者做一件不可思议的事：主动攀谈。他们让芝加哥火车上的通勤者与同车乘客交谈。《纽约时报》总结道：“当艾普利博士和施罗德女士请同一车站的其他人预测与陌生人交谈后会有什么感受时，通勤者们认为独自坐着会让这趟车程更愉快。”尽管参与者没指望有什么好的体验，但当他们真的完成了实验，“没有一个人说感到尴尬。”

事实上，据报道，有过交流的通勤比没有交流的更愉快，这完全在情理之中，因为人类靠社交联结滋养。正所谓：跟陌生人聊聊天，能让你感到不再孤单。

2016 年　考研英语二完型真题

Happy people work differently. They're more productive, more creative, and willing to take greater risks. And new research suggests that happiness might influence firms work, too.

Companies located in places with happier people invest more, according to a recent research paper. , firms in happy places spend more on R&D (research and development). That's because happiness is linked to the kind of longer-term thinking for making investments for the future.

The researchers wanted to know if the and inclination for risk-taking that come with happiness would the way companies invested. So they compared U.S. cities' average happiness by Gallup polling with the investment activity of publicly traded firms in those areas.

enough, firms' investment and R&D intensity were correlated with the happiness of the area in which they were . But is it really happiness that's linked to investment, or could something else about happier cities why firms there spend more on R&D? To find out, the researchers controlled for various that might make firms more likely to invest – like size, industry, and sales – and for indicators that a place was to live in, like growth in wages or population. The link between happiness and investment generally even after accounting for these things.

The correlation between happiness and investment was particularly strong for younger firms, which the authors to "less codified decision making process" and the possible presence of "younger and less managers who are more likely to be influenced by sentiment." The relationship was stronger in places where happiness was spread more . Firms seem to invest more in places where most people are relatively happy, rather than in places with happiness inequality.

this doesn't prove that happiness causes firms to invest more or to take a longer-term view, the authors believe it at least at that possibility. It's not hard to imagine that local culture and sentiment would help how executives think about the future. "It surely seems plausible that happy people would be more forward-thinking and creative and R&D more than the average," said one researcher.

快乐的人工作方式不同。他们效率更高，更有创造力，也更愿意承担更大的风险。而新的研究表明，快乐还可能影响公司的运作方式。

据最近一篇研究论文，位于人们幸福感更高的地方的公司投资更多。具体来说，幸福地区的公司在研发（研究与开发）上花得更多。这是因为幸福与着眼长远的思维方式有关，而这种思维正是为未来投资所必需的。

研究人员想知道，幸福带来的乐观情绪和冒险倾向是否会改变公司的投资方式。于是，他们把盖洛普民调测得的美国各城市平均幸福感，与这些地区上市公司的投资活动做了对比。

果然，公司的投资和研发强度与所在地区的幸福感相关。但究竟是幸福本身与投资相关，还是幸福城市的其他因素解释了这些公司研发投入更高的原因？为了弄清楚，研究人员控制了可能促使公司投资的各种因素——如规模、行业和销售额——以及能说明一个地方宜居的指标，如工资或人口增长。即使考虑了这些因素，幸福与投资之间的关联总体上依然成立。

幸福与投资的相关性在年轻公司中尤为显著，作者将其归因于“不太成文的决策流程”，以及可能存在的“更年轻、经验更少、更容易受情绪影响的管理者”。在幸福感分布更均匀的地方，这种关系也更强。公司似乎更愿意在大多数人相对幸福的地方投资，而不是在幸福感不均的地方。

尽管这并不能证明幸福导致公司增加投资或采取更长远的眼光，作者认为它至少暗示了这种可能性。不难想象，当地文化和情绪会影响高管对未来的思考。“快乐的人更有前瞻性、更有创造力、更倾向于在研发上投入，这似乎是顺理成章的，”一位研究人员说。

2017 年　考研英语二完型真题

People have speculated for centuries about a future without work. Today is no different, with academics, writers, and activists once again that technology is replacing human workers. Some imagine that the coming work-free world will be defined by : A few wealthy people will own all the capital, and the masses will struggle in an impoverished wasteland.

A different and not mutually exclusive holds that the future will be a wasteland of a different sort, one by purposelessness: Without jobs to give their lives , people will simply become lazy and depressed. , today's unemployed don't seem to be having a great time. One Gallup poll found that 20 percent of Americans who have been unemployed for at least a year report having depression, double the rate for Americans. Also, some research suggests that the for rising rates of mortality, mental-health problems, and addiction poorly-educated, middle-aged people is a shortage of well-paid jobs. Perhaps this is why many the agonizing dullness of a jobless future.

But it doesn't follow from findings like these that a world without work would be filled with unease. Such visions are based on the of being unemployed in a society built on the concept of employment. In the of work, a society designed with other ends in mind could strikingly different circumstances for the future of labor and leisure. Today, the of work may be a bit overblown. "Many jobs are boring, degrading, unhealthy, and a waste of human potential," says John Danaher, a lecturer at the National University of Ireland in Galway.

These days, because leisure time is relatively for most workers, people use their free time to counterbalance the intellectual and emotional of their jobs. "When I come home from a hard day's work, I often feel ," Danaher says, adding, "In a world in which I don't have to work, I might feel rather different" – perhaps different enough to throw himself a hobby or a passion project with the intensity usually reserved for matters.

几个世纪以来，人们一直在猜想没有工作的未来。今天也不例外，学者、作家和活动家们再次警告：技术正在取代人工。有人想象，即将到来的无工作世界将被不平等定义：少数富人将拥有全部资本，大众则在贫困的荒原中挣扎。

另一种并不互斥的预测认为，未来将是另一种荒原，一种以空虚无意义为特征的荒原：没有工作赋予人生意义，人们只会变得懒惰抑郁。的确，如今的失业者似乎过得并不开心。一项盖洛普民调发现，失业至少一年的美国人中有20%表示患有抑郁症，是有工作者的两倍。此外，一些研究表明，受教育程度低的中年人死亡率上升、心理健康问题和成瘾问题的解释，是缺少高薪工作。也许这就是为什么许多人担忧无工作未来的那种煎熬般的沉闷。

但由这些发现并不必然推出：没有工作的世界会充满不安。这种悲观设想基于“在建立在就业观念之上的社会中失业的弊端”。在没有工作的情况下，一个以其他目标设计的社会，可能为劳动与休闲的未来带来截然不同的境况。如今，工作的美德可能被吹捧得有点过头了。“许多工作枯燥乏味、贬损人格、损害健康，是对人类潜能的浪费，”爱尔兰国立戈尔韦大学讲师约翰·达纳赫说。

如今，由于大多数工人的闲暇时间相对稀缺，人们用空闲时间来平衡工作的脑力与情感消耗。“辛苦工作一天回到家，我常常感到很累，”达纳赫说，又补充道，“在一个不用工作的世界里，我的感觉可能会大不一样”——也许会大不一样，足以让他以通常只为工作事务保留的那种投入强度，全身心投入一项爱好或热爱的事业。

2018 年　考研英语二完型真题

Why do people read negative Internet comments and do other things that will obviously be painful? Because humans have an inherent need to uncertainty, according to a recent study in Psychological Science. The new research reveals that the need to know is so strong that people will to satisfy their curiosity even when it is clear the answer will .

In a series of four experiments, behavioral scientists at the University of Chicago and the Wisconsin School of Business tested students' willingness to themselves to unpleasant stimuli in an effort to satisfy curiosity. For one , each participant was shown a pile of pens that the researcher claimed were from a previous experiment. The twist? Half of the pens would an electric shock when clicked.

Twenty-seven students were told which pens were electrified; another twenty-seven were told only that some were electrified. left alone in the room, the students who did not know which ones would shock them clicked more pens and incurred more shocks than the students who knew what would . Subsequent experiments reproduced this effect with other stimuli, the sound of fingernails on a chalkboard and photographs of disgusting insects.

The drive to is deeply rooted in humans, much the same as the basic drives for or shelter, says Christopher Hsee of the University of Chicago. Curiosity is often considered a good instinct – it can new scientific advances, for instance – but sometimes such can backfire. The insight that curiosity can drive you to do things is a profound one.

Unhealthy curiosity is possible to , however. In a final experiment, participants who were encouraged to how they would feel after viewing an unpleasant picture were less likely to to see such an image. These results suggest that imagining the of following through on one's curiosity ahead of time can help determine it is worth the endeavor. "Thinking about long-term is key to reducing the possible negative effects of curiosity," Hsee says. In other words, don't read online comments.

人们为什么要去看负面的网络评论，还做其他明显会让自己痛苦的事？根据《心理科学》杂志最近的一项研究，因为人类有一种消除不确定性的内在需求。这项新研究表明，求知的需求是如此强烈，以至于人们会想方设法满足自己的好奇心，哪怕明知答案会带来伤害。

在一系列四个实验中，芝加哥大学和威斯康星商学院的行为科学家测试了学生们为了满足好奇心而让自己接触不愉快刺激的意愿。在其中一项试验中，每位参与者面前都放着一堆笔，研究人员声称这些笔来自之前的实验。关键在于：一半的笔在被按下时会释放电击。

二十七名学生被告知哪些笔带电；另外二十七名只被告知有些笔带电。当独自留在房间里时，不知道哪些笔会电到自己的学生按的笔更多，受到的电击也更多，而知道会发生什么的学生则不然。后续实验用其他刺激物重复了这一效应，比如指甲划黑板的声音和令人作呕的昆虫照片。

芝加哥大学的克里斯托弗·西（Christopher Hsee）说，探索的驱动力深深扎根于人类之中，就像对食物或住所的基本需求一样。好奇心常被视为一种好的本能——比如它能带来新的科学进步——但有时这种探究会适得其反。好奇心会驱使你做出自我伤害的事，这一洞见意义深远。

然而，不健康的好奇心是可以抵制的。在最后一项实验中，被鼓励去预测自己看完不愉快图片后会有何感受的参与者，不太可能选择去看这样的图片。这些结果表明，提前想象放任好奇心会带来什么结果，有助于判断是否值得一试。“思考长远后果是减少好奇心可能带来的负面效应的关键，”西说。换句话说，别去看网络评论。

2019 年　考研英语二完型真题

Weighing yourself regularly is a wonderful way to stay aware of any significant weight fluctuations. , when done too often, this habit can sometimes hurt more than it .

As for me, weighing myself every day caused me to shift my focus from being generally healthy and physically active, to focusing on the scale. That was bad to my overall fitness goals. I had gained weight in the form of muscle mass, but thinking only of the number on the scale, I altered my training program. That conflicted with how I needed to train to my goals.

I also found that weighing myself daily did not provide an accurate of the hard work and progress I was making in the gym. It takes about three weeks to a month to notice significant changes in your weight altering your training program. The most changes will be observed in skill level, strength and inches lost.

For these , I stopped weighing myself every day and switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule . Since weight loss is not my goal, it is less important for me to my weight each week. Weighing every other week allows me to observe and any significant weight changes. That tells me whether I need to my training program.

I use my bimonthly weigh-in to get information about my nutrition as well. If my training intensity remains the same, but I'm constantly and dropping weight, this is a that I need to increase my daily caloric intake.

The to stop weighing myself every day has done wonders for my overall health, fitness and well-being. I'm experiencing increased zeal for working out since I no longer carry the burden of a morning weigh-in. I've also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, I'm training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.

Rather than over the scale, turn your focus to how you look, feel, how your clothes fit and your overall energy level.

定期称体重是了解体重明显波动的好方法。然而，如果称得太频繁，这个习惯有时弊大于利。

就我而言，每天称体重让我把注意力从“保持整体健康、积极锻炼”转移到了只盯着体重秤上。这对我的整体健身目标很不利。我的体重增加是以肌肉量的形式增加的，但我一心只想着把秤上的数字降下来，于是改了训练计划。这与我实现目标所需的训练方式相冲突。

我还发现，每天称体重并不能准确反映我在健身房的付出和进步。调整训练计划后，大约需要三周到一个月才能看到体重的明显变化。最先能观察到的变化体现在技能水平、力量和围度的减少上。

出于这些原因，我不再每天称体重，改为每两周称一次。既然减重不是我的目标，每周追踪体重对我就没那么重要了。每两周称一次能让我观察并解释体重的明显变化，从而判断是否需要调整训练计划。

我还用每两周的称重结果来了解自己的营养状况。如果训练强度不变，但我总是饿、体重还在掉，这就是个信号，说明我需要增加每日热量摄入。

停止每天称体重的决定对我的整体健康、体能和幸福感大有裨益。自从不再背负令人失望的晨间称重的负担，我锻炼的热情高涨。在实现具体健身目标上我也更成功了，因为我是按目标训练，而不是按秤上的数字。

与其对着体重秤耿耿于怀，不如把注意力转到你的外形、感觉、衣服合身度和整体精力水平上。

2020 年　考研英语二完型真题

Being a good parent is, of course, what every parent would like to be. But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very , particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting. A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, , a younger sibling.

, there's another sort of parent that's a bit easier to : a patient parent. Children of every age benefit from patient parenting. Still, every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy . Sometimes parents get exhausted and frustrated and are unable to maintain a and composed style with their kids. I understand this.

You're only human, and sometimes your kids can you just a little too far. And then the happens: You lose your patience and either scream at your kids or say something that was a bit too and does nobody any good. You wish that you could the clock and start over, We've all been there.

, even though it's common, it's important to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may for a long time. This may not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also your child's self-esteem.

If you consistently lose your with your kids, then you are inadvertently modeling a lack of emotional control for your kids. We are all becoming increasingly aware of the of modeling tolerance and patience for the younger generation. This is a skill that will help them all throughout life. In fact, the ability to emotionally regulate or maintain emotional control when by stress is one of the most important of all life's skills.

Certainly, it's incredibly to maintain patience at all times with your children. A more practical goal is to try, to the best of your ability, to be as tolerant and composed as you can when faced with situations involving your children. I can promise you this: As a result of working toward this goal, you and your children will benefit and from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally.

当个好父母当然是每个父母都想做到的。但“好父母”意味着什么，这个定义无疑非常棘手，尤其是孩子们对同一种养育方式的反应各不相同。一个冷静、守规矩的孩子，可能对某种养育方式的反应就和比如年幼的弟弟妹妹不一样。

幸运的是，还有一种父母更容易描述：耐心的父母。每个年龄段的孩子都能从耐心的养育中受益。然而，尽管每个父母都想有耐心，这可不是件容易的事。有时父母会精疲力竭、倍感沮丧，无法在孩子面前保持宽容镇定的风格。我理解这种感受。

人非圣贤，有时孩子们真会把你逼到极限。然后不可避免的事就发生了：你失去耐心，要么冲孩子大吼，要么说了些有点太刻薄的话，对谁都没好处。你多希望能让时光倒流、重新来过。我们都有过这种时候。

然而，尽管这很常见，也要记住：在疲惫的一瞬间，你可能对孩子说出让自己后悔很久的话。这不仅会伤害你和孩子的关系，还会影响孩子的自尊。

如果你总对孩子发火，你就在无意中给孩子树立了情绪失控的榜样。我们越来越意识到，为年轻一代树立宽容和耐心的榜样有多重要。这是一项能让他们受益终生的技能。事实上，在面对压力时调节情绪、保持情绪控制的能力，是人生最重要的技能之一。

当然，时刻对孩子保持耐心非常难。更实际的目标是：尽你所能，在面对和孩子有关的棘手情况时，尽量宽容镇定。我可以向你保证：朝着这个目标努力，你和孩子都会受益，会从紧张时刻中走出来，身心感觉更好。

2021 年　考研英语二完型真题

It's not difficult to set targets for staff. It is much harder, , to understand their negative consequences. Most work-related behaviors have multiple components. one and the others become distorted.

Travel on a London bus and you'll see how this works with drivers. Watch people get on and show their tickets. Are they carefully inspected? Never. Do people get on without paying? Of course! Are there inspectors to that people have paid? Possibly, but very few. And people who run for the bus? They are . How about jumping lights? Buses do so almost as frequently as cyclists.

Why? Because the target is . People complained that buses were late and infrequent. , the number of buses and bus lanes were increased, and drivers were or punished according to the time they took. And drivers hit these targets. But they hit cyclists. If the target was changed to , you would have more inspectors and more sensitive pricing. If the criterion changed to safety, you would get more drivers who obeyed traffic laws. But both these criteria would be at the expense of time.

There is another : people became immensely inventive in hitting targets. Have you that you can leave on a flight an hour late but still arrive on time? Tailwinds? Of course not! Airlines have simply changed the time a is meant to take. A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight.

The of the story is simple. Most jobs are multidimensional, with multiple criteria. Choose one criterion and you may well others. Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a . Setting targets can and does have unforeseen negative consequences.

This is not an argument against target-setting. But it is an argument for exploring consequences first. All good targets should have multiple criteria critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback. The trick is not only to just one or even two dimensions of the objective, but also to understand how to help people better the objective.

给员工定目标不难。难得多的是理解定目标带来的负面后果。大多数工作行为都有多个维度。强调其中一个，其他方面就会扭曲。

坐一趟伦敦公交，你很快就会明白这在司机身上是怎么应验的。看人们上车出示车票。有人认真查票吗？从不。有人逃票上车吗？当然！有稽查员检查人们是否付钱吗？可能有，但很少。追公交的人呢？司机根本不理。闯红灯呢？公交车闯红灯跟骑车人一样频繁。

为什么？因为目标是准时。人们抱怨公交晚点、班次太少。于是，公交车数量和公交专用道增加了，司机按耗时被奖励或惩罚。司机们达到了这些目标。但他们也撞了骑车的人。如果目标改成收入，就会有更多稽查员和更灵活的票价。如果标准改成安全，你会得到更多遵守交规的谨慎司机。但这两个标准都会以牺牲时间为代价。

还有另一个问题：人们在达标上变得极富“创造力”。你有没有注意到，航班能晚起飞一小时却准点到达？是顺风吗？当然不是！航空公司只是改了一段旅程本该花的时间。一小时的航程现在按两小时来算。

这个故事的寓意很简单。大多数工作都是多维的，有多个标准。选定一个标准，很可能牺牲其他标准。一切都可以更快、更便宜，但这是有代价的。定目标会带来意想不到的负面后果。

这不是反对定目标，而是主张先探究后果。所有好的目标都应有多重标准，涵盖时间、金钱、质量、客户反馈等关键因素。诀窍不仅在于明确目标的一两个维度，还在于懂得如何帮助人们更好地实现目标。

Harlan Coben believes that if you're a writer, you'll find the time; and that if you can't find the time, then writing isn't a priority and you're not a writer. For him, writing is job—a job like any other. He has it with plumbing, pointing out that a plumber doesn't wake up and say that he can't work with pipes today.

, like most writers these days, you're holding down a job to pay the bills, it's not to find the time to write. But it's not impossible. It requires determination and single-mindedness. that most bestselling authors began writing when they were doing other things to earn a living. And today, even writers who are fairly often have to do other work to their writing income.

As Harlan Coben has suggested, it's a of priorities. To make writing a priority, you'll have to some of your day-to-day activities and some things you really enjoy. Depending on your and your lifestyle, that might mean spending less time watching television or listening to music, though some people can write they listen to music. You might have to the amount of exercise or sport you do. You'll have to make social media an activity rather than a daily, time-consuming . There'll probably have to be less socializing with your friends and less time with your family. It's a learning curve, and it won't always make you popular.

There's just one thing you should try to keep at least some time for, your writing—and that's reading. Any writer needs to read as much and as widely as they can; it's the one supporter—something you can't do without.

Time is finite, the older you get, the it seems to go. We need to use it as carefully and as as we can. That means prioritizing out activities so that we spend most time on the things we really want to do. If you are a writer, that means——writing.

哈兰·科本认为，如果你是个作家，你总能挤出时间；如果你挤不出时间，那就说明写作并非你的优先事项，你也算不上真正的作家。对他而言，写作是正常的工作——和其他工作没什么两样。他曾把写作比作水管工，指出水管工不会一觉醒来就说今天没法跟水管打交道了。

如果你和如今大多数作家一样，得靠一份工作糊口，那么想挤出时间写作并不容易。但也并非不可能，这需要决心和专注。记住，大多数畅销书作家都是在靠别的工作谋生时开始写作的。如今，即使是相当知名的作家，也常常要靠其他工作来补贴写作收入。

正如哈兰·科本所说，这是个优先次序的问题。要把写作列为优先事项，你就得牺牲一些日常活动和真正喜欢的事。根据你的兴趣和生活方式，这可能意味着少看电视、少听音乐——尽管有些人听着音乐也能写作。你可能得削减锻炼或运动的时间，得把社交媒体变成偶尔为之的活动，而不是每天耗时耗力的习惯。跟朋友的聚会大概要减少，陪家人的时间大概也要减少。这是个艰难的学习曲线，也不会总让你受欢迎。

只有一件事，你应该尽量留出一些时间，除了写作之外——那就是阅读。任何作家都需要尽可能多读、尽可能广读；这是唯一不可或缺的支撑，缺了它万万不行。

时间是有限的，年纪越大，时间似乎过得越快。我们要尽可能谨慎而高效地利用时间。这意味着给各项活动排出优先次序，把大部分时间花在真正想做的事上。如果你是作家，那就意味着——最重要的是——写作。

And improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.

Things changed, , when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard, a growth team and sparked the kind of perspective they needed. By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered.

Armed with this , the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently the premium version to users of the free version. , upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.

But in order for your growth team to succeed, it needs to have a strong leader. It needs someone who can the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement. This leader will the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the of these goals.

The growth leader is also for keeping the team focused on moving forward and steering them clear of distractions. attractive new ideas can be distracting, the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't the current goal and need to be put on the back burner.

这是当今许多创业者都会遇到的常见情形：你是小公司的首席执行官，虽然赚得不错，却需要找到办法让公司更上一层楼。你要做的是通过组建增长团队来优先发展增长业务。增长团队由公司各部门成员组成，借助协作的力量专注于寻找增长之道。

来看一个现实中的例子。在组建增长团队之前，软件公司 BitTorrent 有五十名员工，分属工程、市场和产品开发等传统部门。这曾带来不错的业绩，直到二〇一二年增长停滞。问题在于，太多客户用的是基础免费版。尽管对付费高级版做了不少改进，升级的人却寥寥无几。

情况有了转机，一位富有创意的项目营销经理加入，组建了增长团队，带来了他们急需的全新视角。从营销角度看工程问题，很快发现升级者寥寥并非质量问题——大多数客户只是不知道有高级版，也不知道它有什么功能。

但要让增长团队成功，必须有强有力的领导者。需要有人能团结跨学科团队，让他们不偏离改进方向。这位领导要明确目标领域，设定清晰目标，并为实现这些目标制定时间表。

增长负责人还负责让团队专注前行、不被杂事分心。尽管诱人的新想法可能分散注意力，团队领导必须识别出哪些想法与当前目标不相关，把它们暂时搁置。

Your social life is defined as the activities you do with other people for pleasure, when you are not working. It's important to have a social life, but what's right for one person won't be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, , some of us may feel drained, even if it's doing something we enjoy.

This is why finding a in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not others, can make you feel lonely and . Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, you are working from home and you are on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can periods of loneliness too, such as retirement changing jobs or becoming a parent. It's important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to a social life, but it can feel overwhelming . It's a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet people. There are groups aimed at new parents and those who want to a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and ideas.

On the other hand, it's possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you're always doing something and there is never any in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social . We all have our own social limit and it's important to recognise when you're feeling like it's all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be of poor social health. Make sure you some time in your diary when you're for socialising and use this time to relax, and recover.

社交生活指的是工作之余和他人一起做的娱乐活动。社交生活很重要，但适合一个人的不一定适合另一个人。有的人和别人在一起待久了精力充沛，而有的人却觉得被掏空，哪怕做的是自己喜欢的事。

所以在社交生活中找到平衡很关键。独处太久、不见他人，会让人感到孤独疏离。孤独会影响心理健康，还会导致情绪低落。任何人都可能在任何时候感到孤独。比如，如果你在家办公，错过了办公室里日常的社交闲聊，这种感觉可能更强烈。退休、换工作、为人父母等人生变化也会引发一段孤独期。重要的是正视这种孤独感。有办法重拾社交生活，但起初可能让人望而却步。好的起点是想想自己喜欢的爱好，然后找到相关的社群和活动，在那里结识志同道合的人。有针对新手父母的社群，有供人第一次尝试新运动的活动，也有同行交流想法的社交晚会。

另一方面，社交生活也可能过度。如果总在忙，日程里从来没有休息的空档，就可能社交倦怠、社交疲惫。每个人的社交上限不同，要觉察何时觉得超载了。情绪低落、没精神、易怒、失眠都可能是社交健康不佳的征兆。一定要在日记本里划出一段时间，在你不参加社交的时候用它来放松、休息、恢复。

You might have about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with. someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts. Yet another that might be worried about is being a nuisance or the person you go to for help.

If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to for help because you have the added worry of the other person your request. Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves. And while you might coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are as more competent, not less.

Perhaps most encouraging of all is a paper from 2022 by researchers at Stanford University that involved a mix of contrived help-seeking interactions and asking people to times they'd sought help in the past. 需要帮助时难以开口，背后的原因很多都可以理解。心理学家几十年来一直对这个问题感兴趣，尤其因为人们普遍不愿求助，已导致一些引人注目的失败。

求助需要勇气。你要说出自己的需求——有你做不到的事。换句话说，你等于在广播自己的弱点，这会让人不舒服。你可能担心显得无能，可能担心失去对求助事项的掌控。一旦有人开始帮忙，没准他会接管一切，或抢走你之前的功劳。另一个让人顾虑的因素是：怕打扰人家、给人家添麻烦。

如果你自卑，求助可能更难，因为你还多一层担心：对方拒绝你的请求。你可能把拒绝解读为关系不妙的信号。要克服这些困难，提醒自己人人有时都需要帮助。没人无所不知、无所不能。你可能害怕显得无能，但研究表明，求助者反而被视为更有能力，而非更无能。

最鼓舞人心的是一项斯坦福大学二〇二二年的研究，混合了设计好的求助互动和让人回忆过去求助的经历。结果发现，求助者普遍低估别人愿意帮忙的程度，也低估帮忙带给助人者的好心情（对多数人来说，能帮别人是高度有回报感的）。

所以下次需要求助时记住这些，另外，注意找对人、选对时机。如果对方此刻帮不上，别往心里去——他们可能只是太忙，或对自己能不能帮上没信心。

Most of us strive for self-respect — to see ourselves in a positive light, to be of who we are. Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only to want to avoid them. But the thing is, your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective. Much of it comes down to your of what someone said or did.

When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person. Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a member of staff. Or, two of your friends cancel your get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you. Psychologists have a for this way of thinking: personalisation.

But the is that your boss might view you very highly. It's just you made some in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time. , in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just their minds.

In both — and others that we all experience — there's another at work that psychologists call mind reading. This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you, when you can't really know without them directly.

One simple way to avoid personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's . When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you — especially in the sense of saying anything deep or about you.

When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes. The fact your boss took the time to give you at all means they care enough to want to help you . When it comes to your friends — maybe it's because your friendship is so that they felt able to cancel at late notice.

我们大多追求自尊——积极看待自己，为自己的样子感到自豪。任何打击自尊的评价或经历都会让人不舒服，想要回避也再自然不过。但问题是，自尊是否真的被打击了，很大程度上是主观的，很大程度上取决于你对别人言行的看法。

把事情往自己身上揽，就是把这些情形解读为对你本人的重大负面评价。比如老板挑你销售报告的毛病，你就觉得她认为你是个差劲的员工；或者两个朋友取消了跟你在酒吧的计划好的聚会，你就解读为他们烦你了。心理学家给这种思维起了个术语：个人化。

但事实是，老板可能很器重你；只是报告里有些错误，她指出来是想让你下次做得更好。同样，朋友取消聚会，没准那周末他俩都不舒服，或者只是改变主意了。

这两个例子——以及我们都会遇到的其他情形——背后还有另一种心理机制在起作用，心理学家称之为读心术：你自以为知道别人怎么想你，其实不直接问本人根本无从得知。

避免陷入个人化和读心术的一个简单办法，是挑战你对“已发生之事”的负面假设。当你又往自己身上揽时，试着想想不那么以自我为中心的解读——尤其别往深了想，别觉得这说明你这个人有什么根本问题。

这么做时，换位思考会有帮助。老板肯花时间给你反馈，说明他在乎你、想帮你进步。至于朋友——没准正因为你们友谊足够牢固，他们才敢临时取消。

“Reskilling” is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future in which a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 percent of the “core skills” within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline.

The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company that decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy, though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.

With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 percent and 5.5 percent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the U.S. were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 percent and 13.7 percent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.

Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks. But even if you cannot close the gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 percent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university. 3 https://

“再培训”听起来像个流行词，但如果你希望未来大量潜在劳动者不被落下，它其实是一种必需。我们知道，我们正进入一个时期：热门工作会迅速变化，现存工作的要求也会变。世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，岗位内“核心技能”平均有42%会发生变化。时间非常紧迫。

谁来为再培训买单，是个棘手的问题。对单个公司来说，诱惑总是存在的：裁掉技能不再吃香的员工，换上有需求技能的人。但事情并不总是这样。AT&T常被视为标杆，它决定大规模搞再培训项目，而不是采取裁员再招人的策略。其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。不过，当技能错配是整个经济层面的问题时，人们通常指望政府来处理。加拿大等地的努力充其量只能说是不温不火，结果就是我们经常听到：即便在失业率高的时期和地区，雇主也在抱怨招不到人。

疫情之下，失业率确实很高。二月份，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于代际低点，用工荒遍地都是。到五月份，这两个数字飙升到13.3%和13.7%，虽然很多用工荒消失了，但并非全部。以医疗领域这个明显的例子来说，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医务人员依然明显短缺。

当然，你不可能让一个失业的服务员几周内就培训成医生。但即便填不上这个缺口，也许能填上别的，而这对各方都有好处。瑞典似乎就是个例子：北欧航空被迫让90%的机舱员工休假时，决定启动一个短期再培训项目，把这些员工培训去支援医院工作人员。这一行动是集体协作，还有其他公司和一所瑞典大学参与。

With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines. In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.

Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food. The country produces only about 60 percent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s. A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation’s health. Sounds great — but how feasible is this vision?

According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 percent of the country’s total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. That supplies 80 percent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn’t allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.

There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave. To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively — meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.

But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn’t help. There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn’t have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. Just 25 percent of the country’s land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields. Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg — which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes — we would achieve only a 30 percent boost in crop production.

Just 23 percent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home- grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 percent of our fresh produce needs. That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake. 5 https://

到2050年全球人口预计接近100亿，一些地区的农业产量需要翻番才能跟上，粮食安全越来越成为头条话题。在英国，这最近也成了热议话题，原因还挺特别：脱欧。

一些人把脱欧视为扭转英国食品进口趋势的机会。英国只生产其消费食品的约60%，低于上世纪80年代末的近四分之三。支持者认为，重回自给自足能提振农业、增强政治主权，甚至有益国民健康。听起来很美，但这个愿景可行吗？

利兹大学关于英国食品生产的报告显示，英国85%的国土与肉奶生产相关。这供应了消费量的80%，所以即便把全国都变成畜牧场，也满足不了全部肉奶需求。

这些数字有很多附加条件，但依然严峻。要大幅提高自给率，英国得大幅减少动物性食品消费，还可能要更集约地耕作，意味着更少的绿色田野、更多的工厂化生产。

但转向以植物为主的饮食也帮不上忙。英国以畜牧业为主是有充分理由的：大部分土地的土壤或气候不适合商业化种植。只有25%的国土适合种庄稼，其中多数已被耕地占用。即便把所有适宜土地都改种果蔬，那得铲掉所有自然保护区、让成千上万人搬家，作物产量也只能提高30%。

英国消费的果蔬目前只有23%是本土种植，所以即便采取最极端的措施，也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。这还没算种谷物、糖、籽、油所需的土地，而这些提供了我们目前热量摄入的绝大部分。

Text 3

When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked up two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley. Microsoft’s own Office dominates the market for “productivity” software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.

Both apps, however, were later scrapped after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products. Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many “acqui-hires” that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.

To Microsoft’s critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path. “They bought the seedlings and closed them down,” complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors. Microsoft declined to comment.

Like other start-up investors, Mr Arnold’s own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: “I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on. But are they good for the American economy? I don’t know.”

The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question. This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade. Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.

Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals — many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise — might seem beside the point. Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years — a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year. 7 https://

However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a “buy and kill” tactic to simply close them down.

2015年微软收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和手机日历Sunrise时，拿下的是两个在硅谷声名鹊起的新秀。微软自家的Office主导着生产力软件市场，但这些初创公司代表了一波新技术浪潮，从零开始为智能手机时代打造。

但两款应用后来都被砍掉了，微软称已把它们最好的功能用在了自家产品里。两支工程师团队留了下来，成为大公司用来满足技术人才饥渴的众多收购式招聘之一。

在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运，是大型科技公司无情吞噬挡路创新公司的例证。他们买下幼苗然后掐死，旧金山Switch Ventures的合伙人Paul Arnold抱怨道，终结了那些有朝一日可能成为竞争对手的企业。微软拒绝置评。

和其他初创投资人一样，Arnold的生意也常常靠把初创公司卖给大科技公司，不过他承认对此心情复杂：自私点说，这对我有好处。但对美国经济有好处吗？我不知道。

美国联邦贸易委员会说想找到这个问题的答案。本周，它要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年众多小额收购的信息。虽然目前只是调研，但这一要求让人看到监管者介入早期科技市场的可能，此前这些市场一直在其触及范围之外。

考虑到五家公司合计市值超过5.5万亿美元，翻查这些小交易，很多比Wunderlist和Sunrise还不起眼，似乎有点小题大做。五家大公司过去五年在10亿美元以下收购上年均仅花费34亿美元，对其巨额储备和去年美国1300多亿美元的风险投资来说九牛一毛。

但批评者说，大公司利用这类交易，在最具威胁的潜在竞争对手还没机会起势之前就买下，有时干脆是买下即掐死的策略。

Text 4

We’re fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to a five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive. In one study of the ability she called “thin slicing” the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor’s overall effectiveness. Their ratings correlated strongly with students’ end-of-semester ratings. Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory. Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.

Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating. Accuracy dropped dramatically. Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression. She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.

Other research shows we’re better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection. “It’s as if you’re driving a stick shift,” says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, “and if you start thinking about it too much, you can’t remember what you’re doing. But if you go on automatic pilot, you’re fine. Much of our social life is like that.”

Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences. College students’ ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts’ opinions when the students weren’t asked to analyze their rationale. And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex — when they had a lot of information to process.

Intuition’s special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances. In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech). Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition (“gut feelings,” “hunches,” “my heart”). Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest. 9 https:// Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.

我们挺擅长凭第一印象判断人，从瞥一眼照片到五分钟的接触，这些短暂体验的信息量很小，而深思熟虑不仅多余，还可能添乱。已故心理学家Nalini Ambady在一项她称为薄片的研究中，让参与者看教授10秒钟的无声视频片段，给老师的总体教学效果打分。他们的评分与学生学期末的评分高度相关。另一组参与者在看片段时要从1000开始倒数九，占用有意识的工作记忆，评分同样准确，证明了这种社交处理的直觉性。

关键的是，还有一组被要求先花一分钟写下判断理由再打分，准确率大幅下降。Ambady怀疑，深思熟虑让他们聚焦于生动但误导的线索，比如某些手势或措辞，而不是让微妙信号的复杂互动形成整体印象。她在另一项实验中发现了类似的干扰：参与者看两人15秒片段，判断他们是陌生人、朋友还是情侣。

其他研究表明，靠直觉而非反思，我们更擅长从短暂接触中识破欺骗。东北大学心理学家Judith Hall说：就像开手动挡，你越琢磨越记不清自己在干嘛；挂自动挡反而没事。我们的社交生活很多时候就这样。

想太多也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。大学生在不被要求分析理由时，给草莓酱和大学课程的评分与专家意见更吻合。人们在被要求关注感受而非细节时，买车决策客观上更好、个人也更满意，但只在决策复杂、信息量大的情况下。

直觉的特殊威力只在特定条件下释放。一项研究中，参与者完成八项任务，其中四项考反思性思维，辨规则、理解词汇，四项考直觉和创造力，想新产品、想比喻。然后他们评估自己在多大程度上用了直觉。不出所料，用直觉损害了前四项的表现，但帮助了后四项。

Text 1

On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown’s 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas. Some rest in the shade of a parked car. Others drink water with the cows. This all seems random, but it’s by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.

These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they’re also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture — special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases. Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.

“I’m excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver-based NestFresh Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat. The birds’ waste then fertilizes fields. Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.”

The egg industry’s push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering. In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart. More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories. If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.

Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine. Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say their eggs have more protein).

The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability. Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment. Young adults “really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations. “They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even if they understand what they’re doing.” 3 https://

最近一个晴朗的日子，13000只鸡在得克萨斯州Shiner的Larry Brown的40英亩大风农场上溜达。有的在停着的汽车阴影里休息，有的和牛一起喝水。看似随意，实则精心设计，这是价值61亿美元的美国鸡蛋产业押注的下一个大卖点：气候友好型鸡蛋。

这些鸡蛋现在以每打最高8美元的价格上架，仍贴着有机和动物友好的标签，但产蛋的鸡生活在使用再生农业的农场，用特殊技术培育能锁住温室气体的肥沃土壤。这类鸡蛋可以作为助力应对气候变化来营销。

我对我们的进展很兴奋，为丹佛NestFresh Eggs供蛋的Brown说，他正在增加覆盖作物，引来蚯蚓和蟋蟀给鸡吃。鸡粪接着肥田。这些改进让母鸡能觅食到更高质量的天然饲料，对土地、母鸡和我们供给消费者的鸡蛋都有好处。

蛋鸡业的这波操作，是检验再生农场动物产品能否成为下一个高端品类的首次大考。十多年前，有机鸡蛋还被当作天然食品店里的小众产品，如今已进驻沃尔玛。益生菌和植物肉当初也有类似质疑，但都爆发成了超市大品类。如果可持续鸡蛋推广成功，可能为再生牛肉、西兰花等打开闸门。

再生产品可能不好卖，因为这个概念很难三言两语讲清，宾州州立大学农业经济学副教授Julie Stanton说。这类耕作对食品本身的改善也微乎其微，虽然有生产商说自家鸡蛋蛋白质更高。

行业押注的是：愿意为散养、非转基因、牧场鸡蛋等高端属性多花钱的消费者，也会拥抱可持续。调查显示年轻一代更关心气候变化，植物肉的部分成功就归功于消费者想表达环保意愿。年轻人真的在乎地球，Egg Innovations总裁John Brunnquell说，他们正在改变食物链，程度超出我的想象，哪怕他们自己都没意识到。

Text 2

More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.

One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade. Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees” — those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring — said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.

Financial needs aren’t the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend. Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression. About 72% of “unretire” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.

“The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade. “It’s not just about finances. The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”

One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer. The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 3.2% from the prior year, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. That’s also up 30.2% since 2010. Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations. The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades. About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.

Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2,000 adults between 40 to 79. Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey. Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts. Seniors are living longer, but planning for the extended years is key.

Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, 5 https:// a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth. He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.

“The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said. “It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one. Many people believe they can’t retire.”

越来越多美国人选择工作到退休之后，这一趋势可能颠覆旧的劳动力模式。

TD Ameritrade委托Harris Poll的调查显示，三分之一40岁以上的美国人退休后有工作或计划工作，以应对更长的人生。更惊人的是，超过一半的不退休者，那些计划退休后工作或退休后重返职场的人，说即便钱够养老，晚年也会工作。

不退休潮不只是缺钱。研究显示其他原因包括个人满足感：保持头脑灵活、打发无聊、避免抑郁。约72%的不退休受访者说退休后重返工作是为了保持头脑灵活，59%说与维持生计有关。

TD Ameritrade退休业务高级经理Christine Russell说：退休的概念在演变，不只是钱的问题，工作的价值也在推动人们退休后继续工作。

退休模式变化的原因之一：美国人更长寿。2018年65岁以上人口占16%，比上年增长3.2%，比2010年增长30.2%。老年人口也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体，婴儿潮一代预计比上一代更长寿。过去三十年，劳动年龄人口中退休年龄段的比例翻了一番。今年二月65岁以上人口中20%在工作，高于1985年1月10%的历史最低点。

因为寿命延长，美国人也在多存钱保住养老本。调查显示，六成不退休者为更长的人生增加储蓄，最流行的方式是减少开支、买人寿保险、多缴退休账户。活得久，但为延长的岁月规划是关键。

但Facet Wealth联合创始人Brent Weiss说，很多选择退休后工作的人是在为晚年入不敷出而担心。他建议准退休者找理财顾问定长期财务目标。

Weiss说：人生最难的时刻是结婚、生子，最终是退休。这不只是财务决定，也是情感决定。很多人觉得自己退不起休。

Text 3

We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives. Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless signup process but was later difficult to cancel. Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice. These are examples of dark patterns.

First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users. Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel,” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.

In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices. Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood. Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.

Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns? Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company’s user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions. Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.”

Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level. In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.” The regulations aim to ban dark patterns — this means prohibiting companies from using “confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn’t opt out.”

As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community. Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards. 7 https://

我们都遇到过：会员或订阅注册时丝滑顺畅，取消时却难如登天。本该简单透明的事，被有意无意地复杂化，损害消费者选择。这些就是暗黑模式。

暗黑模式2010年由用户体验专家Harry Brignull首创，是个统称，指操纵用户界面、影响用户决策能力的做法。Brignull归纳了12种常见暗黑模式，从误导、隐藏费用，到蟑螂旅馆，开头体验轻松直觉，想退出时却难如登天。

2019年一项针对53000个产品页和11000个网站的研究发现，约十分之一采用了这类设计。暗黑模式虽普遍，概念仍不被充分理解。企业和非营利组织领导者应了解暗黑模式，避开它制造的灰色地带。

道德的说服性设计和暗黑模式的界限在哪？企业应组织IT、合规、风控、法务团队审查隐私政策，讨论还要叫上负责用户界面的体验设计师和程序员，以及负责注册、购物车、定价和促销的市场和广告人员。这些团队都可能参与制造或避免数字欺骗。

立法者和监管者开始慢慢处理暗黑模式的模糊地带，最近到了州一级。三月，加州总检察长宣布批准《加州消费者隐私法案》附加法规，确保消费者行使数据隐私权时不被混淆误导。法规旨在禁用暗黑模式，即禁止公司使用混淆性语言或不必要步骤，比如逼用户点好几个页面或听一堆别退订的理由。

随着更多州考虑出台法规，商界需要更强的内部问责。暗黑模式也可以靠自律解决，但前提是企业自我约束，不只满足法律要求，还要遵守行业最佳实践和标准。

Text 4

Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports. But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.

The researchers investigated one class session’s impact on eating meat. They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students’ attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering. Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory- farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion. The other half focused on charitable giving instead. Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester — nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students. “It’s an awesome data set,” says Nina Strohminger, a psychologist who teaches business ethics at the University of Pennsylvania and was not involved in the study.

Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books. But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent — and this effect held steady for the study’s duration of several weeks. Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.

“That’s actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says. Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable. And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.”

Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence — classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common. Second, the video may have had an emotional 9 https:// impact. Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role. Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants’ eating habits and students’ video exposure. Meanwhile Schwitzgebel — who had predicted no effect — will be eating his words.

虽然世界各地都有伦理课，但科学家不确定这些课真能改变行为；两方面的证据都很弱，靠的是刻意设计的实验室测试或有时不可靠的自我报告。但《Cognition》发表的一项新研究发现，至少在一个真实场景中，一节伦理课可能产生了持久影响。

研究者考察了一节课对吃肉行为的影响。加州大学河滨分校哲学家、合著者Eric Schwitzgebel说选这个行为有三个原因：学生在这话题上态度多变不稳定；行为容易测量；伦理学界基本认同少吃肉是好事，减少环境伤害和动物痛苦。四门哲学大课的一半学生读了工厂化养殖肉类伦理的文章，可选看了11分钟视频并参加50分钟讨论；另一半则讨论慈善捐赠。随后在学生不知情的情况下，研究者分析了他们那学期的匿名饭卡消费，近500名学生近14000张小票。没参与研究的宾大商学院伦理学心理学家Nina Strohminger说：这数据太棒了。

Schwitzgebel预测干预无效；他以前发现伦理学教授在投票率、献血、还图书馆书等一系列行为上并不比其他教授强。但讨论过肉类伦理的学生中，含肉餐食购买从52%降到45%，效果在几周的研究期内保持稳定；另一组维持在52%。

干预这么小，效果居然这么大，Schwitzgebel说。没参与研究的Strohminger说她希望效果是真的，但不能排除某个未知的混杂变量；即便为真，她指出，另一个轻推可能逆转它：来得容易去得快。

Schwitzgebel怀疑最大影响来自社会影响，带讨论的同学或助教可能分享了自己的素食，展示其可行或普遍。其次视频可能有情感冲击。他认为最没劲的是理性论证，虽然合著者说理性作用可能更大。现在研究者在深挖教学风格、助教饮食习惯、学生视频观看量的具体影响。而当初预测无效的Schwitzgebel，要食言了。

Text 1

In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut — and it is the environment that is paying the price. About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year’s event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.

Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: “We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic. We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.”

The RHS’s decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes. A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers. It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns. They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.

However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.

In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has “no plans to ban the use of artificial grass.”

It added: “We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters. However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives.” 3 https://

在追求完美草坪的过程中，全国各地的房主都在走捷径——而付出代价的是环境。每年约有800万平方米的塑料草皮售出，但反对之声如今已蔓延到园艺界最高层。切尔西花展已宣布从今年起禁用假草，称其不符合花展的精神。主办方皇家园艺学会（RHS）表示，之所以出台禁令，是因为塑料草皮对环境和生物多样性造成破坏。

RHS 的埃德·霍恩说："我们去年启动了可持续发展战略，假草与我们的精神和对塑料的看法完全不符。我们建议使用真草，因为它有益环境，包括为野生动物提供栖息地、缓解洪涝、给环境降温。"

在 RHS 作出这一决定的同时，活动人士正努力提高人们对假草危害的认识。一个自称要"戳破人造草皮的绿色谎言"的推特账号已有超过2万粉丝。它正呼吁人们签署两份请愿书，一份要求禁止销售塑料草皮，另一份要求对这类草坪征收"生态破坏"税。两份请愿书已分别征集到7276个和11282个签名。

然而，假草的支持者指出，天然草坪也有环境代价，天然草坪需要修剪，因此通常耗电或耗油。行业还指出，真草需要大量浇水、除草剂或其他养护，而铺设假草的人往往更常使用自家花园。行业还声称，铺设假草的人平均会在花园的树木或灌木上花费500英镑，为昆虫提供栖息地。

去年，针对另一份要求禁用假草坪的请愿书（征集到3万个签名），政府回应称"没有计划禁用人造草皮"。

政府补充道："我们更愿意帮助人们和机构做出正确选择，而不是在这些问题上立法。不过，人造草皮的使用必须遵守现有的法律和政策保障措施，以保护生物多样性、确保可持续排水，同时，强化的生物多样性义务等措施应能鼓励公共机构考虑可持续的替代方案。"

Text 2

It’s easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government’s ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it’s a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?

But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.

But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.

Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.

The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. We conducted a comprehensive survey examining how U.S. residents view their national parks, and we found that Americans place a very high value on them — whether or not they actually visit them. The peer-reviewed economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers, conducted by mail and internet, also found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.

The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America’s past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites — including Ellis Island and Gettysburg — and to bring the stories of these places to life.

The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system — an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) 5 https:// with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009 as part of the Obama stimulus package. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

把联邦政府为填补国家公园长期资金缺口而想出的点子斥为荒谬，实在太容易了。真有人觉得允许亚马逊把包裹送到你在约塞米蒂的帐篷、让餐车在红杉国家公园的红杉树下排起长队是好主意吗？

但政府有一点说对了：美国国家公园确实陷入危机。它们总计有超过120亿美元的维修欠账，道路、步道、洗手间、游客中心等基础设施都在年久失修。

但把营地私有化、商业化并非万能药。营地只占基础设施欠账总额的一小部分，而园内企业平均只把约5%的收入上交给国家公园管理局。

而且，更多的私有化无疑会削弱每年3亿游客来公园的主要原因之一：享受自然、暂时摆脱淹没日常生活的商业喧嚣。

真正的问题在于，公园长期资金匮乏。我们做了一项全面调查，了解美国居民如何看待国家公园，发现无论是否亲自到访，美国人都高度重视国家公园。这项针对700名纳税人的同行评议经济调查（通过邮件和网络进行）还发现，人们愿意花一大笔钱确保公园及其项目完好无损。约81%的受访者表示，愿意在未来10年多缴税，以避免国家公园被削减开支。

国家公园对美国居民价值巨大，既是逃离喧嚣之地，也是自然的象征。此外，它们还通过广泛的教育项目、通过碳封存对气候的积极影响、对文化艺术生活的贡献，当然还有旅游业创造价值。公园还有助于留住美国的历史，与全国数千个地方司法管辖区合作保护历史遗迹——包括埃利斯岛和葛底斯堡——让这些地方的故事重焕生机。

公园用少得可怜的经费做着这一切。国会每年只给国家公园系统拨款30亿美元——按实际购买力算，这个数字自2001年以来就没变过（2009年奥巴马刺激计划中的一次性追加除外）。与此同时，年游客量自1980年以来增长了50%以上，如今达到每年3.3亿人次。

Text 3

The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain,” for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn’t remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.

In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading.” Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking — something that is not available on the Internet. “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things,” Sparrow says, adding that we haven’t lost our ability to do it.

Still other experts say it’s too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.

“There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I’d have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. “It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don’t know.” 7 https://

哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝齐·斯帕罗认为，互联网改变的可能只是我们记住什么，而非我们的记忆能力。2011年，斯帕罗主导了一项研究：让参与者在电脑上记录40条冷知识（比如"鸵鸟的眼睛比它的大脑还大"）。一半参与者被告知信息会被删除，另一半被告知会被保存。结果如何？后者在之后测验时根本没费心去记，因为他们知道能在电脑上找到。在同一项研究中，还有一组被要求既记住信息又记住存放的文件夹。他们没记住信息，但记住了怎么找到文件夹。换句话说，人类的记忆不是在退化，而是在"适应新的通信技术"，斯帕罗说。

从非常实际的角度看，互联网正在成为我们记忆的外接硬盘，这一过程被称为"认知卸载"。过去，这个角色由数据库、图书馆和其他人承担。比如你父亲可能永远记不住生日，因为你母亲记得。有人担心这会对社会产生破坏性影响，但斯帕罗看到了积极面。她认为，这一趋势或许会把我们的学习方式从聚焦单个事实和死记硬背，转向更强调概念性思维——而这是在互联网上找不到的。"我个人从不觉得死记硬背有多大智力价值，"斯帕罗说，并补充道我们并没有丧失这种能力。

还有一些专家说，现在断言互联网如何影响大脑还为时过早。心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·西蒙斯写道，没有实验证据表明它会干扰我们的专注力，比如。2008年加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学与人类行为研究所一项针对24名参与者的研究还发现，会用电脑的老年人在上网时大脑比阅读时更活跃。

"我们越来越依赖互联网可能是有代价的，但我猜总体上好处会大于代价，"心理学教授本杰明·斯托姆说。"记忆显然在变化，但它是向好的方向变吗？目前我们还不知道。"
